title: Minimum Relay Packs
src: Walmart OA, IIT BHU. Coding question 1 of 3.
body:
A campus shuttle travels forward along a straight route from position 0 to position L. It starts with enough battery to cover distance S, so it can reach any position up to S.

There are m relay stations on the route, given in increasing order of position. Station j is at M[j][0] and holds one battery pack that adds M[j][1] to the shuttle's reach. The shuttle can collect a pack only once it has reached that station (the station's position is at most the current reach). Each pack can be collected at most once, and the shuttle may collect a pack it does not immediately need. Collecting never reduces the reach.

Return the minimum number of packs the shuttle must collect to get its reach to at least L, or -1 if that is impossible.

Function to complete

Complete minRelayPacks(L, M, S). It returns the minimum number of packs, or -1.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: First line: L m. Then m lines, each with position gain. Last line: S.
out: One integer: the minimum number of packs, or -1.
cons: 0 ≤ position < L, positions in increasing order
the reach can exceed 32 bits; use 64-bit arithmetic

samples.ex: Reach starts at 3. Take the pack at 2 (+3): reach 6. Take the pack at 5 (+4): reach 10 >= L. Two packs.
The only station is at 5 but the reach is 4, so its pack can never be collected.

spec.returns: the minimum number of packs, or -1

wrong.why: takes the smallest pack instead of the largest
treats a station exactly at the current reach as out of reach (< instead of <=)
takes every reachable pack in order instead of choosing

    _raw = sys.stdin.read(); _t = _raw.split(); _p = 0
    L = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _m = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    M = [list(map(int, _t[_p + _i * 2:_p + (_i + 1) * 2])) for _i in range((_m))]; _p += (_m) * 2
    S = int(_t[_p]); _p += 1
    _r = Solution().minRelayPacks(L, M, S)
    print(_r)
